recipes.title: Scrambled Eggs with Spinach
recipes.desc: Fluffy eggs with wilted spinach — simple, fast and protein-rich.
steps: Whisk eggs with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add spinach and wilt for 1 minute.
Pour in eggs and scramble gently on low heat until just set.
recipes.benefits: Eggs are one of the most complete protein sources, containing all essential amino acids. Spinach adds iron, folate, and vitamin K with almost zero calories.

recipes.title: Banana Pea Protein Smoothie
recipes.desc: Thick, creamy smoothie with pea protein and banana. Ready in minutes.
steps: Add all ingredients to blender.

Blend until smooth.
Add ice if desired.
recipes.benefits: Pea protein is highly digestible and rich in BCAAs for muscle recovery. Banana provides fast-releasing carbohydrates and potassium for muscle function.

recipes.title: Rice Cake with Almond Butter & Banana
recipes.desc: Crunchy rice cakes topped with almond butter and fresh banana slices.
steps: Spread almond butter evenly over rice cakes.
Top with banana slices and serve immediately.
recipes.benefits: Almond butter provides healthy monounsaturated fats and vitamin E. Banana offers natural sugars and potassium. A quick, energising start to the day.

recipes.title: Yoghurt with Berries & Chia Seeds
recipes.desc: Creamy lactose-free yoghurt layered with berries, chia seeds and honey.
steps: Spoon yoghurt into a bowl.
Top with berries, chia seeds and a drizzle of honey.
recipes.benefits: Chia seeds are loaded with omega-3 fatty acids and fibre. Berries are among the highest antioxidant foods available, supporting cellular repair and inflammation reduction.

recipes.title: Overnight Oats with Pea Protein
recipes.desc: No-cook overnight oats with pea protein. Prep tonight, grab tomorrow.
steps: Mix all ingredients together in a jar.
Refrigerate overnight.
Top with fresh fruit before eating.
recipes.benefits: Oats are rich in beta-glucan, a soluble fibre that lowers LDL cholesterol and stabilises blood sugar. Combined with protein, this keeps you full for hours.

recipes.title: Egg & Avocado Bowl
recipes.desc: Poached eggs over halved avocado with chili and lemon. Zero cooking skill required.
steps: Poach or boil eggs to your preference.
Halve avocado and season with lemon juice, chili flakes and salt.
Serve eggs on top of avocado halves.
recipes.benefits: Avocado is rich in monounsaturated fats and potassium — more than bananas. Combined with eggs, this delivers sustained energy and excellent satiety.

recipes.title: Mango Coconut Smoothie Bowl
recipes.desc: Thick blended mango and coconut base topped with granola. Tropical and filling.
steps: Blend mango, protein and coconut milk until thick and smooth.
Pour into a bowl and top with granola and coconut flakes.
Serve immediately.
recipes.benefits: Mango is high in vitamin C and digestive enzymes. Coconut milk provides MCTs metabolised rapidly for energy, making this a great pre-workout breakfast.

recipes.title: Turkey & Egg Breakfast Bowl
recipes.desc: Savory turkey and egg scramble with bell pepper. High protein, minimal carbs.
steps: Brown turkey with paprika in olive oil over medium heat, about 4 minutes.
Push turkey aside and scramble eggs in the same pan.
Add diced pepper, mix everything together and serve.
recipes.benefits: Ground turkey is one of the leanest protein sources. Bell peppers contain more vitamin C than oranges, supporting immune function and iron absorption.

recipes.title: Sweet Potato & Egg Hash
recipes.desc: Crispy sweet potato hash with eggs baked right in. One pan, zero fuss.
steps: Fry diced sweet potato in olive oil over medium heat for 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden.
Make two wells in the hash and crack in the eggs.
Cover the pan and cook 3 minutes until eggs are just set.
recipes.benefits: Sweet potato is loaded with beta-carotene, an antioxidant that converts to vitamin A. Its lower glycaemic index versus regular potato means slower, more sustained energy.

recipes.title: Savory Rice Congee with Egg
recipes.desc: Silky rice porridge in bone broth with a soft-cooked egg. Warming and easy to digest.
steps:
Bring broth to a boil.
Add rice and simmer 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until porridge-like.
Crack eggs directly into the congee and stir gently — they will poach in about 2 minutes.
Finish with sesame oil and spring onions.
recipes.benefits: Bone broth is rich in collagen, glycine, and minerals that support gut lining integrity. Rice congee is one of the most easily digestible meals you can make.

recipes.title: Tuna & Brown Rice Bowl
recipes.desc: Canned tuna over brown rice with cucumber and a soy sauce (gluten-free) sesame dressing.
steps: Drain tuna thoroughly and mix with soy sauce (gluten-free) and sesame oil.
Serve over rice with sliced cucumber alongside.
recipes.benefits: Canned tuna is one of the most cost-effective lean protein sources. Brown rice adds complex carbohydrates and manganese for bone health and energy metabolism.

recipes.title: Chicken & Roasted Veg Bowl
recipes.desc: Pan-fried chicken breast with Italian-seasoned roasted vegetables.
steps:
Toss vegetables with half the oil and herbs.
Roast at 200°C for 20 minutes.
Pan-fry chicken in remaining oil, 6 minutes per side until cooked through.
Slice chicken and serve over roasted vegetables.
recipes.benefits: Chicken breast is the gold standard for lean protein. Roasting vegetables concentrates nutrients and develops natural sweetness without adding calories.

recipes.title: Red Lentil Soup
recipes.desc: Hearty red lentil soup with cumin. Meal-preps well for 3 days.
steps: Sauté onion and garlic in a drizzle of oil for 3 minutes.

Add lentils, cumin and broth.
Bring to a boil.

Simmer 25 minutes until lentils are soft.
Blend half for a creamy-chunky texture.
recipes.benefits: Red lentils are extraordinarily nutrient-dense — high in plant protein, iron, folate, and fibre. They reduce cholesterol and stabilise blood sugar effectively.

recipes.title: Prawn & Avocado Salad
recipes.desc: Cooked prawns over mixed greens with avocado and a simple lemon dressing.
steps: Toss greens with olive oil and lemon juice.
Top with prawns and sliced avocado.
Season with salt and pepper.
recipes.benefits: Prawns are extremely lean — nearly all calories from protein. Avocado adds heart-healthy fats and folate, making this a nutritionally complete light meal.

recipes.title: Chicken & Edamame Rice Bowl
recipes.desc: Shredded chicken and edamame over rice with a soy sauce (gluten-free) and sesame finish.
steps: Warm chicken and edamame in a pan or microwave.
Serve over rice.
Drizzle with soy sauce (gluten-free) and finish with sesame seeds.
recipes.benefits: Edamame is one of the few plant foods that is a complete protein. Combined with chicken this bowl is very high in protein while remaining low in saturated fat.

recipes.title: Sardine & Cucumber Rice Cakes
recipes.desc: Canned sardines and cucumber on crispy rice cakes with lemon. No cooking needed.
steps: Drain sardines and flake over rice cakes.
Top with cucumber slices, lemon juice and black pepper.
recipes.benefits: Sardines are one of the richest sources of omega-3 fatty acids and vitamin D. Their soft bones also provide calcium, supporting bone density.

recipes.title: Chickpea & Spinach Stew
recipes.desc: Chickpeas simmered in spiced tomato sauce with wilted spinach.
steps: Sauté garlic in a little oil for 1 minute.

Add diced tomatoes, chickpeas and cumin.
Simmer 15 minutes.

Stir in spinach and cook until wilted.
Season and serve.
recipes.benefits: Chickpeas are high in both protein and fibre, making them uniquely satiating. Spinach adds vitamin K, which works synergistically with the iron in legumes.

recipes.title: Vietnamese-Style Prawn Noodle Salad
recipes.desc: Cold rice vermicelli with prawns, fresh mint, and a light fish sauce dressing.
steps: Soak vermicelli in boiling water for 4 minutes, drain and rinse cold.
Toss noodles with prawns, mint, lime juice and fish sauce.
Serve immediately.
recipes.benefits: Fresh mint is surprisingly rich in antioxidants and aids digestion. Fish sauce adds umami depth and trace minerals with minimal calories.

recipes.title: Egg & Veggie Fried Rice
recipes.desc: Classic fried rice with egg, peas and soy sauce (gluten-free) — best made with leftover cold rice.
steps:
Heat a wok or large pan very hot.
Stir-fry cold rice in sesame oil for 2 minutes.
Push rice aside, scramble eggs in the gap.
Add peas and soy sauce (gluten-free), toss everything together for 2 more minutes.
recipes.benefits: Cold rice has higher resistant starch content, acting as a prebiotic with a lower glycaemic impact than freshly cooked rice.

recipes.title: Turkey Lettuce Wraps
recipes.desc: Spiced ground turkey spooned into crisp butter lettuce cups. Low carb and fast.
steps: Brown turkey in a pan with garlic and ginger over medium-high heat.
Season with soy sauce (gluten-free) and cook until liquid reduces slightly.
Spoon into lettuce cups and serve immediately.
recipes.benefits: Lettuce wraps eliminate refined carbs while keeping the meal filling. Ground turkey is exceptionally lean and cooks fast, making this ideal for quick lunches.

recipes.title: Baked Salmon with Broccoli
recipes.desc: Omega-3-rich salmon fillet oven-roasted alongside broccoli florets.
steps:
Toss broccoli with half the oil and garlic powder.
Arrange on a baking tray.
Place salmon alongside, drizzle with remaining oil.

Roast at 200°C for 18 minutes.
Squeeze lemon over before serving.
recipes.benefits: Salmon is the best dietary source of omega-3 fatty acids, reducing inflammation and supporting brain health. Broccoli contains sulforaphane, one of the most studied anti-cancer compounds.

recipes.title: Beef & Broccoli Stir-Fry
recipes.desc: Thinly sliced beef seared fast with broccoli in a soy sauce (gluten-free) garlic glaze.
steps: Mix soy sauce (gluten-free) with cornstarch and 2 tbsp water to make a sauce.

Sear beef in a very hot pan for 1–2 minutes.
Set aside.

Stir-fry broccoli and garlic 3 minutes.
Return beef, pour sauce over, toss 1 minute.
recipes.benefits: Beef is rich in creatine, zinc, and B12 — nutrients critical for muscle function. Broccoli's vitamin C increases iron bioavailability from the beef significantly.

recipes.title: Thai Green Chicken Curry
recipes.desc: Fragrant coconut milk curry with chicken thighs and zucchini.
steps: Fry curry paste in a dry pan for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken and cook 3–4 minutes, coating in paste.

Pour in coconut milk.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Add zucchini and cook 5 more minutes.
Season with fish sauce and serve over rice.
recipes.benefits: Coconut milk provides MCTs used directly for energy rather than stored as fat. Green curry paste contains anti-inflammatory lemongrass and galangal.

recipes.title: Lamb Kofta with Salad
recipes.desc: Spiced ground lamb patties grilled and served with a fresh tomato cucumber salad.
steps:
Combine lamb, garlic, spices and parsley.
Mix well and form into 8 oval patties.
Grill or pan-fry on medium-high heat, 3–4 minutes per side.
Serve with diced tomato and cucumber salad.
recipes.benefits: Lamb is rich in conjugated linoleic acid (CLA), linked to reduced body fat. It's also one of the best sources of zinc, essential for testosterone and immune health.

recipes.title: Miso-Glazed Salmon
recipes.desc: Salmon fillets baked under a sweet miso, honey and soy sauce (gluten-free) glaze.
steps: Mix miso, honey, soy sauce (gluten-free) and ginger into a smooth glaze.
Coat salmon fillets generously on top.
Bake at 200°C for 12–14 minutes until glaze is caramelised.
recipes.benefits: Miso is fermented, providing probiotics for gut health. Combined with salmon's omega-3s, this is one of the most well-rounded anti-inflammatory dinners possible.

recipes.title: Chicken Thigh & Sweet Potato Tray Bake
recipes.desc: Chicken thighs and sweet potato chunks roasted together on one tray.
steps: Toss everything with oil and spices.
Spread on a large baking tray in a single layer.
Roast at 200°C for 35 minutes until chicken skin is crispy.
recipes.benefits: Chicken thighs contain more iron and zinc than breast. Sweet potato's beta-carotene is fat-soluble so roasting with olive oil significantly boosts its absorption.

recipes.title: Prawn & Tomato Stew
recipes.desc: Prawns poached in a smoky garlic tomato sauce with fresh parsley.
steps: Sauté garlic and paprika in olive oil for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes.

Add prawns and cook 3 minutes until pink.
Top with parsley.
recipes.benefits: Cooking tomatoes increases lycopene bioavailability. Lycopene is strongly linked to reduced cardiovascular disease risk.

recipes.title: Steak & Asparagus
recipes.desc: Pan-seared sirloin steak with garlic-sautéed asparagus and lemon.
steps:
Sear steak in a hot pan with half the oil, 3 minutes per side for medium.
Rest 5 minutes.
In the same pan, cook asparagus with garlic and remaining oil for 4 minutes.
Slice steak against the grain and serve with asparagus and lemon.
recipes.benefits: Asparagus is one of the best natural sources of folate. Steak provides heme iron, the most bioavailable form of iron available in food.

recipes.title: Egg Drop Soup
recipes.desc: Silky chicken broth with ribbons of egg — one of the fastest nourishing dinners.
steps: Bring broth to a simmer with soy sauce (gluten-free).
Slowly drizzle in beaten eggs while stirring gently — they cook in thin ribbons.
Finish with sesame oil and spring onions.
recipes.benefits: Chicken broth provides electrolytes and glycine. Perfect for nights when you need something light but genuinely nourishing.

recipes.title: One-Pan Harissa Chicken & Chickpeas
recipes.desc: Chicken thighs and chickpeas roasted in harissa with cherry tomatoes.
steps: Rub chicken thighs with harissa paste.
Toss chickpeas and tomatoes with olive oil on a baking tray.
Nestle chicken on top and roast at 200°C for 30 minutes until caramelised.
recipes.benefits: Harissa contains chillies, garlic and cumin — a potent anti-inflammatory trio. Chickpeas absorb the harissa juices and become deeply flavourful.

recipes.title: Edamame with Chili & Sea Salt
recipes.desc: Steamed edamame pods tossed with sea salt and chili flakes. 5 minutes flat.
steps: Microwave edamame with 2 tbsp water, covered, for 4 minutes.
Drain and toss immediately with salt and chili flakes.
Squeeze beans out of the pods to eat.
recipes.benefits: Edamame is one of the most protein-dense plant snacks. High in folate, vitamin K, and isoflavones associated with hormonal balance.

recipes.title: Pea Protein Chocolate Balls
recipes.desc: No-bake oat and pea protein balls with peanut butter and dark chocolate chips.
steps: Mix oats, protein, peanut butter and honey until combined.

Fold in chocolate chips.
Add 1–2 tbsp water if too dry to roll.
Roll into 12 balls and refrigerate 30 minutes.
recipes.benefits: Dark chocolate provides flavanols that improve blood flow and cognitive function. A balanced ratio of protein, complex carbs and healthy fat in one bite.

recipes.title: Hard-Boiled Eggs with Soy sauce (gluten-free) Dip
recipes.desc: Batch-cook hard-boiled eggs and dip them in a sesame soy sauce (gluten-free) sauce.
steps: Place eggs in cold water, bring to boil, cook exactly 9 minutes.

Transfer to ice water immediately.
Peel when cool.
Mix soy sauce (gluten-free), sesame oil and chili flakes as dipping sauce.
recipes.benefits: Eggs are the reference food for protein quality. The yolk contains choline, essential for brain function — a nutrient most people are deficient in.

recipes.title: Rice Cake with Tuna & Avocado
recipes.desc: Tuna and mashed avocado piled onto crispy rice cakes with a sriracha kick.
steps: Mash avocado with lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Mix tuna with sriracha.
Spread avocado on rice cakes, top with tuna and serve immediately.
recipes.benefits: Three macronutrients in perfect balance — complex carbs, lean protein and healthy fats — in under 5 minutes with zero cooking.

recipes.title: Smoked Salmon & Cucumber Rounds
recipes.desc: Thin cucumber rounds topped with smoked salmon and fresh dill.
steps: Slice cucumber into thick rounds.
Top each round with a piece of smoked salmon and a sprig of dill.
Finish with lemon juice and black pepper.
recipes.benefits: A near-zero-carb high-protein snack. Smoked salmon provides the full B vitamin spectrum including B12, essential for neurological function and energy.

recipes.title: Roasted Chickpeas
recipes.desc: Chickpeas roasted until crunchy with smoked paprika and cumin.
steps: Thoroughly pat chickpeas dry — this is key for crunch.
Toss with oil and spices.
Roast at 200°C for 25 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden and crispy.
recipes.benefits: A high-fibre crunchy snack without inflammatory seed oils. Chickpeas are rich in folate and magnesium, supporting muscle recovery and energy metabolism.

recipes.title: Pea Protein Shake
recipes.desc: Pea protein shaken with oat milk, vanilla and honey over ice.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker bottle or blender.

Shake or blend until smooth.
Serve immediately over ice.
recipes.benefits: The fastest protein top-up available. Pea protein is hypoallergenic, easily digested, and high in arginine which supports blood flow and recovery.

recipes.title: Shakshuka
recipes.desc: Eggs baked directly in a cumin-spiced tomato sauce. One pan, big flavour.
steps:
Sauté pepper 3 minutes.
Add tomatoes and spices.
Simmer 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Make 4 wells, crack in eggs, cover and cook 5–7 minutes until whites are set.
recipes.benefits: A one-pan meal packed with lycopene from cooked tomatoes and complete protein from eggs. Naturally GF and dairy-free.

recipes.title: Smoked Salmon & Egg Scramble
recipes.desc: Soft scrambled eggs folded together with smoked salmon and spinach.
steps: Scramble eggs in olive oil over low heat until almost set.
Fold in smoked salmon and spinach in the last minute.
Remove from heat — residual warmth finishes the eggs.
recipes.benefits: Two of the most complete protein sources in one pan. Smoked salmon adds omega-3s while spinach contributes iron and folate for red blood cell production.

recipes.title: Green Detox Smoothie
recipes.desc: Spinach, kale and pea protein blended with banana. A concentrated hit of micronutrients.
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until completely smooth.
Drink immediately for best nutritional value.
recipes.benefits: Kale is pound-for-pound one of the most nutrient-dense foods on earth, rich in vitamins K, C, A and manganese. A concentrated micronutrient delivery system.

recipes.title: Chicken Caesar Salad (GF)
recipes.desc: Grilled chicken over romaine with a simple lemon-dijon dressing. No croutons needed.
steps: Whisk olive oil, lemon juice and mustard together for dressing.
Toss romaine with dressing.
Top with sliced chicken and serve.
recipes.benefits: Romaine lettuce is rich in vitamins A, C and K. The olive oil dressing aids absorption of fat-soluble vitamins in the greens.

recipes.title: Spicy Tuna Cucumber Boats
recipes.desc: Tuna and avocado mix stuffed into halved bell peppers. No cooking needed.
steps: Halve cucumber lengthways and scoop out seeds with a spoon.
Mix tuna with sriracha and sesame oil.
Fill cucumber halves and top with sesame seeds.
recipes.benefits: Almost zero carbs with very high protein. Sriracha contains capsaicin which temporarily boosts metabolism and has antioxidant properties.

recipes.title: Baked Sweet Potato with Tuna
recipes.desc: Baked sweet potato filled with tuna, avocado and lemon. Slow carbs, fast protein.
steps: Bake sweet potato at 200°C for 40 minutes until tender.
Mix tuna with mashed avocado and lemon juice.
Halve the potato and fill with tuna mixture.
recipes.benefits: Baked sweet potato develops natural sweetness as starch converts to sugars. Slow-release carbs paired with lean protein and healthy fat creates excellent blood sugar stability.

recipes.title: Beetroot & Walnut Salad
recipes.desc: Roasted beetroot over greens with walnuts and a balsamic dressing.
steps: Arrange greens on a plate.
Top with sliced beetroot and walnuts.
Dress with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
recipes.benefits: Beetroot is high in dietary nitrates that improve oxygen delivery to muscles. Walnuts are the richest nut source of plant omega-3 fatty acids.

recipes.title: Quinoa & Roasted Veg Salad
recipes.desc: Warm quinoa tossed with olive-oil-roasted zucchini and red onion.
steps: Cook quinoa per packet instructions, about 15 minutes.

Toss zucchini and onion with olive oil.
Roast at 200°C for 20 minutes.
Combine warm quinoa with roasted veg and lemon juice.
recipes.benefits: Quinoa is one of the only plant-based complete proteins, containing all nine essential amino acids. Also rich in magnesium and zinc for immune function.

recipes.title: Tofu Scramble
recipes.desc: Crumbled firm tofu scrambled with turmeric and soy sauce (gluten-free) — a plant-based egg alternative.
steps: Crumble tofu with your hands into small chunks.
Fry in olive oil 3 minutes.

Add turmeric and soy sauce (gluten-free).
Stir in spinach until wilted.
recipes.benefits: Tofu contains all essential amino acids and turmeric adds anti-inflammatory curcumin. The soy sauce (gluten-free) provides umami depth without any gluten.

recipes.title: Poached Eggs on Sweet Potato Rosti
recipes.desc: Crispy sweet potato rosti topped with poached eggs and fresh chives.
steps: Squeeze as much moisture as possible from grated sweet potato.
Form into two patties and fry in oil 4 minutes per side until golden.

Poach eggs 3 minutes.
Serve on rosti with chives.
recipes.benefits: Sweet potato rosti is a naturally GF alternative to hash browns. Beta-carotene and fibre make this a nutritionally superior breakfast base.

recipes.title: Mango & Coconut Chia Pudding
recipes.desc: Chia seeds soaked overnight in coconut milk, topped with fresh mango.
steps: Mix chia seeds with coconut milk, vanilla and honey.
Refrigerate overnight — the seeds will swell into a thick pudding.
Top with fresh mango and serve.
recipes.benefits: Chia seeds absorb up to 12x their weight in liquid, forming a gel that slows digestion and stabilises blood sugar throughout the morning.

recipes.title: Almond & Date Energy Balls
recipes.desc: Blended dates and almonds with cocoa, rolled into bite-sized energy balls.
steps: Blend all ingredients in a food processor until it comes together.
Roll into 12 balls.
Refrigerate 20 minutes before eating.
recipes.benefits: Dates are rich in fibre, potassium, and magnesium. Almonds provide vitamin E and healthy fats. A clean pre-workout energy source with no refined sugar.

recipes.title: Blueberry Pea Protein Smoothie
recipes.desc: Frozen blueberries and pea protein blended with oat milk and almond butter.
steps: Blend all ingredients until smooth.
Serve immediately.
recipes.benefits: Blueberries have the highest antioxidant content of any common fruit — rich in anthocyanins linked to improved memory, reduced blood pressure, and eye health.

recipes.title: Baked Eggs in Tomato Sauce
recipes.desc: Eggs baked in a spiced tomato sauce — GF shakshuka at its simplest.
steps: Simmer tomatoes with garlic and cumin 10 minutes.
Make 4 wells and crack in eggs.

Cover and cook 5–7 minutes until whites are set.
Top with parsley.
recipes.benefits: Cooked tomatoes in oil dramatically increase lycopene absorption. A naturally GF and dairy-free one-pan breakfast with complete protein from eggs.

recipes.title: Pineapple Turmeric Smoothie
recipes.desc: Pineapple and coconut smoothie with pea protein and anti-inflammatory turmeric.
steps: Blend all ingredients until completely smooth.
Serve over ice.
recipes.benefits: Pineapple contains bromelain, a digestive enzyme that aids protein absorption. Turmeric's curcumin is one of the most potent natural anti-inflammatory compounds.

recipes.title: Warm Quinoa & Poached Egg
recipes.desc: Warm quinoa with poached eggs over wilted spinach. Nutrient-dense and fast.
steps: Cook quinoa 15 minutes per packet.
Poach eggs 3 minutes in simmering water.

Wilt spinach in olive oil.
Serve eggs over quinoa and spinach with lemon.
recipes.benefits: Quinoa is the only grain-like food that is a complete protein. Its magnesium content combined with egg's choline is particularly beneficial for brain function.

recipes.title: Prawn & Mango Salad
recipes.desc: Cooked prawns with fresh mango over greens with a chili lime dressing.
steps: Toss greens with lime juice.
Add prawns and mango.
Finish with chili flakes and a drizzle of olive oil.
recipes.benefits: Mango and lime together create a vitamin C powerhouse that dramatically increases iron absorption from the prawns. Natural sweetness with excellent protein.

recipes.title: Asian Slaw with Sesame Dressing
recipes.desc: Shredded red cabbage and carrot with a soy sauce (gluten-free) sesame dressing.
steps: Shred cabbage and grate carrots into a bowl.
Toss with soy sauce (gluten-free), sesame oil and rice vinegar.
Let sit 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.benefits: Red cabbage contains 10x more vitamin C than green and is rich in anthocyanins — purple antioxidants linked to brain protection and reduced inflammation.

recipes.title: Chicken & Avocado Lettuce Cups
recipes.desc: Shredded chicken mixed with avocado and cumin, served in lettuce cups.
steps: Mash avocado with lime juice and cumin.
Mix in shredded chicken.
Spoon into lettuce cups and serve.
recipes.benefits: Zero refined carbs, maximum protein and healthy fats. Avocado's oleic acid is the same fat in olive oil, strongly associated with reduced cardiovascular risk.

recipes.title: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Soup
recipes.desc: Blended sweet potato and black bean soup with cumin and lime.
steps: Roast sweet potato at 200°C for 20 minutes.
Blend with broth and cumin until smooth.

Stir in black beans and heat through.
Finish with lime juice.
recipes.benefits: Sweet potato and black beans together provide beta-carotene, folate, magnesium, and sustained energy from complex carbs and fibre.

recipes.title: Sardine & Tomato Salad
recipes.desc: Flaked sardines over sliced tomatoes and red onion with olive oil and lemon.
steps: Slice tomatoes and onion and arrange on a plate.
Flake sardines over the top.
Dress with olive oil and lemon juice.
recipes.benefits: Lycopene from tomatoes is absorbed more efficiently alongside the healthy fats in sardines. A cheap, nutritional powerhouse of a lunch.

recipes.title: Roast Beef & Rocket Salad
recipes.desc: Sliced roast beef over peppery rocket with cherry tomatoes and balsamic.
steps: Plate rocket with cherry tomatoes.
Layer sliced roast beef on top.
Dress with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
recipes.benefits: Rocket is one of the most nutrient-dense salad greens, high in nitrates that improve oxygen efficiency during exercise. A quick high-protein lunch with minimal prep.

recipes.title: Cod with Roasted Tomatoes
recipes.desc: Flaky cod pan-fried and served with burst cherry tomatoes, garlic and basil.
steps: Roast tomatoes and garlic with olive oil at 200°C for 15 minutes.
Season cod and pan-fry 3 minutes per side.
Serve cod with roasted tomatoes and fresh basil.
recipes.benefits: Cod is an exceptionally lean white fish with a very high protein-to-calorie ratio. It's also a good source of iodine, supporting thyroid function and metabolism.

recipes.title: Pork Tenderloin with Green Beans
recipes.desc: Lean pork tenderloin pan-seared and oven-finished, served with steamed green beans.
steps: Sear pork in oil 3 minutes per side until browned.
Transfer to oven at 180°C for 12 minutes.

Steam green beans 4 minutes.
Rest pork 5 minutes before slicing.
recipes.benefits: Pork tenderloin is one of the leanest cuts of any meat, comparable to chicken breast in fat content. Green beans are rich in vitamin K and silicon for connective tissue health.

recipes.title: Beef & Vegetable Soup
recipes.desc: Slow-simmered beef chunks in a hearty GF bone broth with carrots and celery.
steps: Brown beef in batches in a little oil.
Add vegetables and broth.
Bring to boil then simmer 30 minutes until beef is tender.
recipes.benefits: Simmered beef releases collagen into the broth, supporting joint health. Carrots and celery provide beta-carotene and vitamin C.

recipes.title: Baked Trout with Lemon & Dill
recipes.desc: Trout wrapped in foil with lemon slices and dill — moist, delicate and effortless.
steps:
Place each fillet on foil.
Layer with lemon slices and dill.
Drizzle with olive oil and wrap tightly.
Bake at 190°C for 15 minutes.
recipes.benefits: Trout has an excellent omega-3 profile similar to salmon. Dill contains monoterpenes that activate the liver's detoxification enzymes.

recipes.title: Chicken & Mushroom Soup
recipes.desc: Shredded chicken breast and mushrooms in a simple thyme-scented broth.
steps: Sauté onion and mushrooms 5 minutes.
Add chicken, broth and thyme.

Simmer 20 minutes.
Remove chicken, shred, and return to soup.
recipes.benefits: Mushrooms are the only non-animal food naturally producing vitamin D. They also contain beta-glucans that significantly enhance immune response.

recipes.title: Coconut Chicken Soup
recipes.desc: Thai-inspired chicken soup in coconut broth with ginger and lemongrass.
steps: Simmer broth with lemongrass and ginger 5 minutes.
Add coconut milk and bring to gentle simmer.

Add chicken and cook 15 minutes.
Remove lemongrass before serving.
recipes.benefits: Lemongrass has strong antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties. Coconut milk provides MCTs for rapid energy without blood sugar spikes.

recipes.title: Teriyaki Salmon Bowl
recipes.desc: Pan-fried salmon basted in a honey soy sauce (gluten-free) glaze, served over steamed rice.
steps: Mix soy sauce (gluten-free) and honey for the glaze.
Pan-fry salmon skin-side down 4 minutes, flip and baste generously with glaze.

Cook 3 more minutes.
Serve over steamed rice with sesame seeds.
recipes.benefits: Honey in the teriyaki glaze caramelises beautifully and provides trace enzymes and antioxidants. Salmon's omega-3s support joint flexibility and skin health.

recipes.title: Stuffed Bell Peppers with Turkey & Rice
recipes.desc: Ground turkey and rice baked inside bell pepper halves with tomato sauce.
steps: Brown turkey with herbs and tomatoes until reduced.
Mix in cooked rice.
Fill halved peppers and bake at 180°C for 25 minutes.
recipes.benefits: Peppers become sweeter and more digestible when baked. Turkey provides tryptophan — the precursor to serotonin — supporting mood and sleep quality.

recipes.title: Spiced Lamb Chops with Spinach
recipes.desc: Cumin-rubbed lamb chops grilled and served alongside garlic-wilted spinach.
steps: Rub lamb chops with cumin and coriander.
Grill 3–4 minutes per side.

Sauté spinach with garlic until wilted.
Serve alongside with lemon.
recipes.benefits: Lamb chops are exceptionally rich in zinc and B12. Cumin has been linked to improved insulin sensitivity. Spinach provides iron that pairs synergistically with the heme iron in lamb.

recipes.title: Prawn Pad Thai
recipes.desc: Rice noodles stir-fried with prawns and egg in a soy sauce (gluten-free) lime sauce.
steps: Soak noodles per packet instructions.

Stir-fry prawns in a hot wok 2 minutes.
Push aside and scramble eggs.

Add drained noodles, soy sauce (gluten-free) and lime.
Toss everything on high heat.
recipes.benefits: A naturally GF version of a classic. Prawns provide selenium and iodine alongside their excellent lean protein profile. Lime juice adds vitamin C and aids digestion.

recipes.title: Zucchini Noodles with Pesto & Chicken
recipes.desc: Spiralised zucchini tossed with GF pesto and grilled chicken breast.
steps: Spiralise zucchini into noodles.
Toss zoodles with pesto in a pan over low heat for 2 minutes.
Top with sliced chicken and cherry tomatoes.
recipes.benefits: Zucchini noodles replace refined pasta with a vegetable providing vitamin B6 and potassium. Basil contains anti-inflammatory eugenol and has antiviral properties.

recipes.title: Mackerel with Sweet Potato Mash
recipes.desc: Crispy pan-fried mackerel served with silky olive oil sweet potato mash.
steps:
Boil sweet potato until tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain and mash with olive oil.
Pan-fry mackerel skin-side down 4 minutes, flip and cook 2 more minutes.
Serve with mash and lemon.
recipes.benefits: Mackerel has the highest omega-3 content of any commonly available fish. Regular consumption is strongly linked to cardiovascular protection and reduced inflammation.

recipes.title: Egg Fried Cauliflower Rice
recipes.desc: Grated cauliflower stir-fried with egg, peas and soy sauce (gluten-free) — a low-carb rice swap.
steps: Grate cauliflower or pulse in food processor into rice-sized pieces.
Stir-fry with garlic in a hot pan 4 minutes.

Push aside, scramble eggs.
Add peas and soy sauce (gluten-free) and toss together.
recipes.benefits: Cauliflower rice has a fraction of the carbs of regular rice. Cauliflower is high in choline and vitamin C, supporting brain health and immunity.

recipes.title: Spiced Turkey Mince with Rice
recipes.desc: Lean ground turkey with cumin, turmeric and garlic over steamed rice.
steps: Cook rice per packet.
Brown turkey with garlic, cumin and turmeric until cooked through.
Serve over rice.
recipes.benefits: Turmeric's curcumin is a powerful anti-inflammatory. Turkey is the leanest ground meat available. This simple bowl covers a large portion of daily protein needs.

recipes.title: Chili Con Carne (GF)
recipes.desc: Classic chili with lean beef and kidney beans — hearty, high-protein and GF.
steps: Brown beef with garlic in a large pan.
Add kidney beans, tomatoes and chili powder.
Simmer 30 minutes until thickened.
recipes.benefits: Combining beef and kidney beans creates a protein powerhouse with complementary amino acid profiles. Kidney beans are one of the best sources of plant-based iron and folate.

recipes.title: Rice Noodle Soup with Chicken
recipes.desc: Chicken breast in ginger bone broth with rice noodles and bok choy.
steps: Bring broth to a simmer with ginger.
Add chicken and cook 8 minutes.
Add noodles and bok choy, cook 3 more minutes until tender.
recipes.benefits: Rice noodles are lighter and easier to digest than wheat noodles. Ginger supports digestive motility and has well-documented anti-nausea properties.

recipes.title: Sesame Tuna Steak
recipes.desc: Sesame-crusted tuna steak seared rare with soy sauce (gluten-free) and lime.
steps: Press sesame seeds firmly onto both sides of tuna steaks.
Sear in a very hot pan 90 seconds per side — keep the centre pink.
Slice and drizzle with soy sauce (gluten-free) and lime.
recipes.benefits: Fresh tuna steak is one of the highest protein foods available. Sesame seeds are rich in calcium, sesamin, and lignans with potent antioxidant effects.

recipes.title: Beef & Spinach Meatballs
recipes.desc: Baked lean beef meatballs with spinach folded in — great with rice or tomato sauce.
steps: Combine all ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Roll into 18 evenly-sized balls.
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until cooked through and lightly golden.
recipes.benefits: Adding spinach to meatballs boosts iron, folate and vitamin K significantly. Baking rather than frying reduces fat content while creating a slightly crisp exterior.

recipes.title: Smoked Paprika Roast Chicken Legs
recipes.desc: Chicken legs rubbed with smoked paprika and garlic, roasted until crispy.
steps: Rub chicken legs with paprika, garlic powder and olive oil.
Roast at 200°C for 40 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.
Squeeze lemon over before serving.
recipes.benefits: Chicken legs contain more iron and zinc than breast. Smoked paprika is rich in capsanthin, an antioxidant carotenoid. The skin provides fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K.

recipes.title: Almond Butter & Apple Slices
recipes.desc: Crisp apple slices for dipping in almond butter — two ingredients, perfectly balanced.
steps: Slice apple into wedges.
Serve with almond butter for dipping.
recipes.benefits: Apples are high in quercetin and pectin, a soluble fibre that feeds beneficial gut bacteria. Almond butter provides vitamin E, magnesium and healthy monounsaturated fats.

recipes.title: Banana & Peanut Butter
recipes.desc: Banana slices dipped in peanut butter. Two ingredients, ready in 2 minutes.
steps: Slice banana.
Dip in peanut butter.
recipes.benefits: Banana's potassium and peanut butter's magnesium together support muscle contraction and recovery — ideal post-training.

recipes.title: Greek-Style Chicken Skewers
recipes.desc: Lemon-oregano marinated chicken cubes grilled on skewers. Pure lean protein.
steps: Marinate chicken in lemon, oregano, garlic and oil for 10 minutes.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill 3 minutes per side until cooked through.
recipes.benefits: Oregano is one of the highest antioxidant herbs by weight, with strong antimicrobial properties. These skewers are virtually pure lean protein with minimal carbs.

recipes.title: Mixed Nuts & Dark Chocolate
recipes.desc: A portioned mix of nuts and 80%+ dark chocolate — satisfying and nutrient-dense.
steps: Portion nuts and chocolate into a small bowl or bag.
Eat slowly and enjoy.
recipes.benefits: Mixed nuts provide selenium (Brazil), magnesium (almonds) and zinc (cashews). Dark chocolate's flavanols improve endothelial function and blood flow.

recipes.title: Cucumber & Dill Smoked Salmon Salad
recipes.desc: Thin cucumber slices layered with smoked salmon and fresh dill with lemon dressing.
steps: Arrange cucumber slices on a plate.
Layer smoked salmon over cucumber.
Top with dill and dress with lemon juice and olive oil.
recipes.benefits: Dill contains monoterpenes that support liver detoxification pathways. An extremely low-carb, high omega-3 salad ready in minutes.

recipes.title: Mango & Lime Sorbet
recipes.desc: Frozen mango blended with lime juice and honey — a naturally dairy-free frozen treat.
steps: Blend frozen mango with lime juice and honey until smooth.
Serve immediately for soft-serve consistency, or refreeze 30 minutes for firmer texture.
recipes.benefits: A naturally dairy-free frozen treat. Mango provides vitamin C, vitamin A and digestive enzymes. Satisfies sweet cravings with whole fruit, not refined sugar.

recipes.title: Watermelon & Mint
recipes.desc: Chilled watermelon cubes tossed with fresh mint and lime juice.
steps: Cube watermelon and place in a bowl.
Tear mint leaves over the top.
Squeeze lime juice over and serve.
recipes.benefits: Watermelon is 92% water and rich in citrulline, an amino acid that improves blood flow and reduces muscle soreness post-exercise.

recipes.title: Silken Tofu Snack Bowl
recipes.desc: Crumbled silken tofu seasoned with lemon, chives and black pepper — a dairy-free alternative to cottage cheese.
steps: Crumble silken tofu into a bowl.
Season with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Top with fresh chives.
recipes.benefits: Silken tofu is an excellent dairy-free high-protein snack. Rich in isoflavones associated with cardiovascular protection and bone density maintenance.

recipes.title: Coconut Rice with Mango
recipes.desc: Jasmine rice cooked in coconut milk, topped with fresh mango and honey.
steps: Cook rice in coconut milk with a pinch of salt and 100ml water.
Fluff with a fork when done.
Serve topped with fresh mango and a drizzle of honey.
recipes.benefits: Coconut milk provides MCTs for quick energy. Mango delivers vitamin C, A and digestive enzymes. An excellent post-workout carb refuel.

recipes.title: Chicken Miso Soup
recipes.desc: Delicate miso broth with sliced chicken breast, silken tofu and spring onions.
steps: Simmer chicken in water 8 minutes.
Remove a ladle of liquid and dissolve miso paste in it, then return to pot — don't boil miso.

Add tofu and spring onions.
Serve immediately.
recipes.benefits: Miso is a fermented food rich in probiotics that support gut health. Silken tofu adds plant protein and isoflavones linked to cardiovascular protection.

recipes.title: Black Bean & Rice Bowl
recipes.desc: Black beans warmed with cumin and lime, served over rice with fresh coriander.
steps: Warm black beans with cumin and lime juice in a pan.
Serve over rice.
Top with fresh coriander.
recipes.benefits: Black beans are exceptionally high in antioxidants and magnesium, which most people are deficient in and which supports muscle recovery.

recipes.title: Tuna Stuffed Capsicum
recipes.desc: Bell pepper halves filled with a tuna and avocado mixture. No cooking needed.
steps: Halve and deseed bell peppers.
Mix tuna with mashed avocado and lemon juice.
Fill pepper halves and season with black pepper.
recipes.benefits: Bell peppers are one of the highest vitamin C foods available. This no-cook meal combines lean protein with anti-inflammatory healthy fats in minutes.

recipes.title: Chicken & Pumpkin Soup
recipes.desc: Blended pumpkin soup with shredded chicken and cumin. Warming and immune-boosting.
steps:
Sauté onion 3 minutes.
Add pumpkin, broth and cumin.
Simmer 20 minutes until pumpkin is tender.

Blend soup.
Add chicken and simmer 10 minutes.
Shred before serving.
recipes.benefits: Pumpkin is extremely high in beta-carotene and very low in calories. Particularly good for immune support in cooler months.

recipes.title: Chicken Tikka (GF)
recipes.desc: Chicken thighs marinated in lactose-free yoghurt and tikka spices, grilled until charred.
steps: Mix yoghurt with spices and lemon juice.
Coat chicken and marinate at least 1 hour.
Grill or bake at 220°C for 20 minutes until charred and cooked through.
recipes.benefits: Turmeric and garam masala create a potent anti-inflammatory combination. Lactose-free yoghurt tenderises the meat while keeping it entirely dairy-free.

recipes.title: Baked Chicken with Lemon & Herbs
recipes.desc: Chicken breasts marinated in lemon, garlic and thyme then simply oven-baked.
steps: Mix lemon juice, zest, garlic, thyme and olive oil.
Coat chicken and marinate 10 minutes.
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until cooked through.
recipes.benefits: Lemon's vitamin C increases iron absorption from the chicken. Thyme contains thymol, a natural antimicrobial compound with potent antioxidant properties.

recipes.title: Pork & Vegetable Stir-Fry
recipes.desc: Thin pork loin strips stir-fried with bok choy and carrot in sesame soy sauce (gluten-free) sauce.
steps: Stir-fry pork in a very hot wok 3 minutes until cooked.
Add bok choy and carrot, stir-fry 3 more minutes.

Add soy sauce (gluten-free) and sesame oil.
Toss and serve.
recipes.benefits: Pork is the richest dietary source of thiamine (vitamin B1), critical for energy metabolism. Bok choy adds calcium and vitamin A with almost no calories.

recipes.title: Baked Cod with Salsa Verde
recipes.desc: Oven-baked cod fillets topped with a vibrant parsley and caper salsa verde.
steps: Blend parsley, capers, olive oil and lemon juice into a chunky salsa verde.
Season cod and bake at 200°C for 14 minutes.
Spoon salsa verde generously over cooked fish.
recipes.benefits: Capers are high in quercetin and rutin — flavonoids with strong antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects. Parsley is exceptionally rich in vitamin K and C.

recipes.title: Beef Bone Broth Bowl
recipes.desc: Shredded beef simmered in bone broth with ginger and spring onions.
steps: Heat broth with ginger.
Add shredded beef and soy sauce (gluten-free).
Serve in a deep bowl topped with spring onions.
recipes.benefits: Bone broth is extraordinarily rich in collagen peptides, glycine and proline. Regular consumption supports joint cartilage, gut lining integrity, and skin elasticity.

recipes.title: One-Pan Chicken & Broccoli
recipes.desc: Chicken breast and broccoli stir-fried with garlic and soy sauce (gluten-free) cornstarch glaze.
steps: Mix soy sauce (gluten-free) and cornstarch with 2 tbsp water.
Stir-fry chicken in a hot pan 4 minutes.

Add broccoli and garlic, cook 3 minutes.
Pour sauce over and toss.
recipes.benefits: One of the highest protein-to-calorie ratio meals possible. Broccoli's vitamin C significantly increases absorption of the chicken's non-heme iron.

recipes.title: Smoked Paprika Roast Chickpeas & Eggs
recipes.desc: Crispy roasted chickpeas with baked eggs in a smoky tomato base.
steps: Fry chickpeas with paprika and oil until beginning to crisp, about 8 minutes.
Add tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
Make 4 wells, crack in eggs, cover and cook 5 minutes until set.
recipes.benefits: A protein and fibre combination that's deeply satisfying. Chickpeas provide slow-release energy while eggs add complete protein and fat-soluble vitamins.

recipes.title: Beef Stir-Fry with Bok Choy
recipes.desc: Thinly sliced beef seared fast with bok choy, garlic and ginger.
steps:
Sear beef in a very hot wok 2 minutes.
Set aside.
Add garlic and ginger, cook 30 seconds.

Add bok choy and soy sauce (gluten-free), stir-fry 2 minutes.
Return beef and toss.
recipes.benefits: Beef is rich in creatine, zinc and B12, critical for muscle function. Bok choy is a cruciferous vegetable high in calcium and vitamin C.

recipes.title: Smoked Salmon Rice Bowl
recipes.desc: Cold rice noodles with smoked salmon, cucumber and a sesame soy sauce (gluten-free) dressing.
steps: Cook rice noodles per packet, drain and rinse cold.
Toss with soy sauce (gluten-free) and sesame oil.
Top with smoked salmon and cucumber.
recipes.benefits: Smoked salmon is rich in omega-3s and vitamin D. Cucumber is 95% water, adding crunch and hydration with essentially no calories.
